messages:
Claire: Quick design sync — I'm thinking of merging the checklist progress bar with the guided tour so that completing a checklist step advances the tour. Might reduce duplication. Thoughts? Maya: Interesting. Could simplify the UI but risk hiding tour context if people skip checklist items. Need clear mapping between tour steps and checklist steps. Kevin: Data: users who use the tour complete onboarding faster, but 40% skip the tour entirely. If we link them, skipping might hurt checklist completion. Maybe keep both but surface a small inline sync indicator: 'This checklist step will advance the tour.' Sam: Accessibility: if the tour auto-advances when a checklist step completes, ensure SR announces the new tour step and move focus appropriately. Also allow users to opt-out of auto-progress in settings. Olivia: Mock: https://figma.com/file/unique/onboard-sync shows a pill 'Sync with tour' toggle in the checklist header. Toggled on by default for first-run users. Claire: Edge case: users on Dedicated/Private often can't access hosted tour assets. If sync is on, we should fall back to checklist-only and surface a tooltip explaining why. Kevin: Telemetry: add events onboarding.surface.sync_toggled and onboarding.path(choice) so we can see opt-out rates and conversion. Create EXP-2021 to test default on vs off. ux-bot: Research note: non-dev roles prefer explicit progress indicators. PMs told us 'I don't like surprises' so auto-advancing might feel unexpected. Suggest default on for devs, off for PMs. Sam: Microcopy: prefer 'Guide me' over 'Sync with tour' — more user-friendly. Also add SR text: 'Guide me: toggle guides that walk you through the console'. Maya: Good call. Let's A/B test default state by role. Kevin will wire role-based default in backend. Claire: Keyboard nav: when tour advances programmatically, don't steal focus from the user unless they triggered the action. Instead announce the new step in an aria-live polite region and provide a 'Jump to step' keyboard shortcut in the palette. Sam: Example snippet for announcement: ```html
// JS: document.getElementById('onboard-announcer').textContent = 'Step 3: Connect a model. Press Enter to open.'; ``` Olivia: Visual note: when sync is active, show a subtle link icon between the tour and checklist items. Also ensure contrast for the pill is >=4.5:1 on dark themes. ux-bot flagged contrast risk. ux-bot: Contrast check: pill color #0A66FF on dark background fails in high-contrast mode. Suggest #0B5FFF or a 1px darker border for focus. Kevin: I'll add EXP-2021 with variants: default_on_by_role, default_off, and visual_indicator_only. Also track whether users dismiss tour entirely (onboard.dismissed). Claire: Small flows: if a user completes a checklist step outside the UI (API or CLI) we should still mark tour as progressed. Add an API hook that pings the onboarding service. Maya: Good point — some SDK quickstarts create resources programmatically. We'll have auth-safe endpoints to mark steps complete. Add acceptance criteria for security review. Sam: Accessibility acceptance: 1) announcements present for programmatic step changes, 2) toggle reachable by keyboard, 3) contrast and focus ring verified in light/dark, 4) screen reader users can opt out. Olivia: I'll update Figma and include the 'Guide me' microcopy + tooltip and upload prototypes for usability testing. ci-bot: CI: branch onboard-sync (build #504) queued. ETA ~8m. :gear: Kevin: I'll add telemetry keys and EXP-2021 to the experiments board. Claire, can you draft a short copy matrix for role-based defaults? Claire: On it — will post in the experiments doc by EOD. Thanks team.
